The check is started when Next.js initializes the Node server. In [`src/instrumentation.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/f9aba8bc-3cc1-4999-a10b-e53ff829dd2e/src/instrumentation.ts), `register()` loads the event handlers and calls `startScheduler()`. Loading [`src/server/services/event-registry.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/f9aba8bc-3cc1-4999-a10b-e53ff829dd2e/src/server/services/event-registry.ts) also imports `notification-service`, which registers the notification fan-out for `issue.overdue`.

[`src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/f9aba8bc-3cc1-4999-a10b-e53ff829dd2e/src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts) calls `tick()` every minute. The overdue job’s cadence is 60 minutes, so `isDue()` makes it eligible about hourly (and on the first tick). `tick()` enqueues it and drains the queue; [`src/server/jobs/queue.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/f9aba8bc-3cc1-4999-a10b-e53ff829dd2e/src/server/jobs/queue.ts) dispatches it to `runOverdueIssueJob()`. There is also a protected manual trigger: `POST` in [`src/app/api/cron/overdue/route.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/f9aba8bc-3cc1-4999-a10b-e53ff829dd2e/src/app/api/cron/overdue/route.ts) checks the cron secret and calls the same job directly.

`runOverdueIssueJob()` in [`src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/f9aba8bc-3cc1-4999-a10b-e53ff829dd2e/src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts) gets up to 50 organization IDs from `usageRepo.listOrgIdsForRollup()`, then calls `issueRepo.listOverdueIssues(orgId, stamp)` for each. In [`src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/f9aba8bc-3cc1-4999-a10b-e53ff829dd2e/src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts), that query keeps issues in the organization that are not archived, have a due date earlier than `now`, and have a status of `backlog`, `todo`, `in_progress`, or `in_review`. That excludes issues without a due date and completed or canceled issues. The job checks for a null due date again before emitting.

The job’s responsibility is to publish the fact that an issue is overdue; it does not decide how to notify someone. It emits `issue.overdue` through [`src/lib/event-bus.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/f9aba8bc-3cc1-4999-a10b-e53ff829dd2e/src/lib/event-bus.ts), which calls the registered subscribers and isolates handler failures. `issue.overdue` is defined in [`src/types/event.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/f9aba8bc-3cc1-4999-a10b-e53ff829dd2e/src/types/event.ts).

To stop later sweeps from announcing the same issue again, `runOverdueIssueJob()` keeps issue IDs in its module-level `reported` set and skips IDs already there. It adds an ID after `emit()` resolves. This is process-lifetime deduplication: it prevents repeats on later sweeps in the same process, but the set is not durable and a server restart clears it. Also, because the event bus handles subscriber errors without rejecting `emit()`, this set does not guarantee that a failed downstream notification write will be retried.

The `issue.overdue` subscriber in `registerFanOut()` in [`src/server/services/notification-service.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/f9aba8bc-3cc1-4999-a10b-e53ff829dd2e/src/server/services/notification-service.ts) ignores unassigned issues. Otherwise it calls `notify()` with the assignee’s user ID and kind `issue_overdue`. `notify()` reads that person’s preference for this organization and notification kind, resolves the allowed channels, and inserts a notification row addressed to that recipient. If there is no preference row, it defaults to `in_app` and `email`; if the person has turned off every allowed channel, no row is created. The preferences are edited through `NotificationPreferencesForm` and `updateNotificationPreferenceAction` in [`src/components/domain/notification/notification-preferences-form.tsx`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/f9aba8bc-3cc1-4999-a10b-e53ff829dd2e/src/components/domain/notification/notification-preferences-form.tsx) and [`src/actions/notifications/update-preferences.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/f9aba8bc-3cc1-4999-a10b-e53ff829dd2e/src/actions/notifications/update-preferences.ts).

For the in-app channel, the row is stored by `insertNotifications()` in [`src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/f9aba8bc-3cc1-4999-a10b-e53ff829dd2e/src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts); the inbox fetches rows for the signed-in user in [`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/inbox/page.tsx`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/f9aba8bc-3cc1-4999-a10b-e53ff829dd2e/src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/inbox/page.tsx), and the bell links to the notifications view.

There is a limit to what “email” means in this path: the overdue fan-out records an email channel choice, but it does not send an immediate overdue email. For `digestOnly` preferences, [`src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/f9aba8bc-3cc1-4999-a10b-e53ff829dd2e/src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts) builds and sends a digest at the organization’s configured digest hour; `sendEmail()` in [`src/server/services/email-service.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/f9aba8bc-3cc1-4999-a10b-e53ff829dd2e/src/server/services/email-service.ts) currently writes the draft to a structured log rather than using an outbound mail transport.
